reading.body:
Jason Smith's AI record holds 14 dated events: five recorded votes and nine campaign contributions, with Amazon and Google committees supplying all the money.

The contributions cluster. Amazon's PAC gave $3,000 in February 2025, $500 and $2,000 on the same day in July 2025, and $2,500 in May 2026. Google's NETPAC gave $5,000 twice in February 2025 and $5,000 twice in March 2025, with two matching negative entries of $-5,000 recorded the same day, which reads as a correction or reversal in the filings rather than new money. The votes run the other direction in time: S. 146 in April 2025, H.R. 1770 in July 2025, H.R. 5764 in January 2026, H.R. 7757 in June 2026. All five are yea votes on suspension motions, the procedure used for bills considered uncontroversial.

For AI specifically, the money is the part that touches compute. Amazon and Google are the two companies most directly exposed to data center construction and the power contracts behind it, and their PACs are the only donors in this record. That does not establish that any vote was cast for a donor, and the page states plainly that date order is not a claim of causation. What it does show is that the same two firms appear on both sides of the ledger, as donors and as the subject of the bills a member votes on.

What this does not tell the reader is what any of the five bills would do. The record gives bill numbers and roll call numbers, not subject matter, so nothing here says whether a vote concerned AI, data centers, or something else entirely. It also does not cover committee work, co-sponsorships, or positions taken outside recorded votes, and it holds no contributions from any donor other than Amazon and Google. Fourteen events over roughly sixteen months is a narrow slice, and the negative Google entries mean the totals cannot be read as simple sums.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Jason Smith: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 14 events.
